project: GPS Triangle — Bill Maisey performance analysis & coaching report
note: Master feature + testing backlog. TDD applies to the build: for each feature, write a failing test (red), implement to green, then flip passes=true and commit test+impl+spec together. Data/analysis features are validated by reconciliation tests (computed values match the authoritative rcmodelspot results and API distance fields). Scaffold captured 2026-09-27 ahead of build; refine before building.

features.description: Fetch competition standings and heat/group tree for the Oschatz 2026 event from the rcmodelspot JSON API
steps: GET /CompetitionGpsTriangle/Results/{guid} and cache raw JSON
Parse standings (38 pilots) and heats -> groups -> per-flight results
Test: Bill's 17 flights are present and his total (12562) and rank (22) reconcile to the standings

features.description: Fetch per-group ~1Hz GPS replay tracks and select Bill plus the same-air group leader per round
steps: For each of Bill's 17 groups, GET /CompetitionGpsTriangle/ReplayGroup/{groupId}
Identify the scoring flight (handle multi-start artefacts) and the top-scoring same-group leader
Test: Bill and leader present in all 17 groups; parsed laps/speed reconcile to the results tree

features.description: Enrich each flight with weather from the Open-Meteo ERA5 archive at the Oschatz coordinates
steps: GET ERA5 hourly (wind, temp, cloud, radiation, cape) for 3-8 Aug 2026, Europe/Berlin
Map each flight's group start time to the nearest hour
Test: every flight has a weather row within the event window; wind cross-checks track drift order-of-magnitude

features.description: Per-round metric bundle (laps, avg speed, entry altitude/speed, energy, thermalling, pacing, line efficiency) for Bill vs same-air leader
steps: Compute metrics from tracks; convert units (groundSpeed km/h, vario, haversine distances)
Test: computed laps and avg speed equal the authoritative results for every flight; distances within ~3% of API distance fields

features.description: Flight-phase decomposition (start / straight / turn / climb) with per-lap time-deficit attribution vs leader
steps: Segment tracks by bearing-rate and vario; separate turnpoint turns from thermal circles by duration/continuity
Attribute per-lap deficit across phases; rank phases by cost to Bill
Test: phase times per flight sum to the motor-off flight duration (within tolerance); speedrun rounds excluded

features.description: Condition-dependence analysis: Bill's within-group (conditions-controlled) score vs wind and thermal-strength proxies, and time-of-day
steps: Join weather to per-flight scores; compute associations with n caveat
Test: correlations computed over the 14 distance rounds; reported as suggestive, not significant

features.description: Week-long progression separating skill (within-group normalised score) from conditions (raw laps)
steps: Order rounds by day/time; trend normalised score and raw laps
Test: rounds ordered chronologically; both series present for all distance rounds

features.description: Single self-contained HTML file, emailable and openable offline, with all data and charts embedded
steps: Generate report/gps-triangle-world-masters-oschatz-2026.html with inline SVG charts and embedded per-round data
Test: no remote script/image/style dependencies required to render; file opens standalone; size reasonable

The Analysis page carries the Overview/Rounds dropdown (Overview default + 17 rounds)

Test: Home holds a summary paragraph and exactly three section links that navigate to Analysis/Recommendations/Innovations

features.description: GPS ground-track chart: the FACTUAL course from the .rct, reconciled with the GPS tracks in ONE consistent equirectangular projection (cos(lat) longitude, identical for course and tracks). GEOMETRY (corrected - it is NOT equilateral): the course is a RIGHT-ISOSCELES triangle - the three turnpoints sit at RADIUS = the .rct 'length' (350 m, NOT the leg) from the start, at bearings {axis, axis+180, axis-90}; the apex is at axis-90 (pointing away from the ground/safety zones - a fixed venue side); the base (hypotenuse, 2xradius = 700 m) runs along the axis with the start at its midpoint; the two legs are radius*sqrt2 (~495 m); perimeter ~1690 m matches the regs lap. Draw the triangle bold, ink, LAST on top with turnpoint dots; the start/finish as a dashed perpendicular line at the start; full-resolution traces at low opacity; North arrow top-right; 100 m scale bar bottom-left; legend inside bottom-right (right-aligned row); wind vector in the right margin with the plot grid/frame sized so the wind arrow sits WITHIN the framed image (not outside the grid); legend/scale/North never overlap the wind vector; legend row spacing keeps swatches and labels from overlapping
steps: Per heat parse the .rct T: header (start, axis, radius); turnpoints = start + radius at {axis, axis+180, axis-90}, apex = axis-90; project course and replay identically; render with the orientation aids

Test (both pilots, thermalling excluded): turn-arc radius from start ~ the .rct length (350 m) within ~15%; flown leg bearings match course-leg bearings within a few degrees; each corner's fitted arc centre within a small margin of the course corner with the pilot apex just OUTSIDE; start-crossing centroid at the course start; projected distance between two .rct coords equals their haversine distance; Bill and leader agree; triangle drawn last; North+scale+legend present and clear of the wind vector

features.description: Per-plot wind annotation: on each GPS-trace plot show a wind vector arrow positioned at the clockface location of the wind source bearing, OUTSIDE the trace box, pointing inward (the direction the wind blows), with a compass+degrees label (e.g. WNW 285) and speed in KNOTS beneath; small but legible; dark grey/off-black
steps: Pass per-round wind (dir/speed) to the ground-track chart; place arrow+label at the bearing's clockface position outside the plot; convert km/h to knots; compute the compass point from the bearing
Test: each ground-track plot renders a wind arrow at the correct clockface position with a knots label; northerly does not collide with the North marker

Test: speed-run altitude traces both start at t=0 (run time); no chart shows large empty offsets from absolute wall-clock

features.description: The 'Energy Management' chart is a stacked dual-panel sharing one x-axis (relative flight time, both pilots overlaid): altitude on top (~80% height) and ground speed beneath (~20%, compressed y), both pilots on both panels. Single figure title 'Energy Management'; NO per-subplot titles (implied by the y-axis labels). Legend only - drop the line-end labels (they duplicate the legend). Solid blue/green series (colourblind-acceptable for the audience; no dashing required). Light smoothing on the spiky speed panel and clipping the end near the last lap/landing are sensible tidy-ups. This REPLACES the standalone altitude plot on EVERY round (endurance and speed) - the only difference for speed runs was that they previously used absolute time; all rounds now use relative flight-time overlay (T0 = start-line crossing). The x-axis spans the full 30-min working window (each trace still ends at that pilot's last turn-point crossing). Otherwise final and approved: design/prototypes/energy_management_v2.html
steps: Refactor altitude_trace into a two-panel chart sharing one bottom x-axis; add compressed speed panel for both pilots
Test: energy figure renders both an altitude panel and a speed panel for both pilots on one shared x-axis; panels do not overlap

features.description: Inline the web fonts (base64 woff2, Latin-subset, only the weights used) so the report is fully self-contained and identical offline, removing the Google-Fonts network dependency, provided the size cost stays modest (~100-200 KB)
steps: Subset Spectral + Source Sans 3 to Latin and the used weights; embed as base64 @font-face; drop the Google-Fonts link
Test: no remote font <link> remains; fonts embedded as data URIs; total added size within budget; report renders offline with the intended fonts

features.description: Per-round view opens (under the summary) with a 'Visual overview of performance' dashboard, then the Energy Management, ground-track and other sections. TOP ROW - four vertical visuals in order: (1) SCORE as a symmetric vertical density/violin of the group field scores in mid-grey, with the winner as a blue line at 1000 and Bill as a green line at his score over the top; (2) ENTRY SPEED, (3) ENTRY ALTITUDE, (4) AVERAGE SPEED (SINGLE-LAP SPEED on speed runs) as BULLET plots - the grey track top is the regs cap where one exists (entry speed 120, entry altitude 400) else a sensible domain max; the leader is a blue line; Bill is the green fill; Bill's value labelled in GREEN to the RIGHT of the bar (not black, not on the bar); NO orange cap line and NO field on the bullets. BOTTOM ROW: LAPS as a small paired bar chart (no axis; value labels on top; Bill green, leader blue); within-group RANK as text (N/field); a WIND compass card (arrow at source bearing blowing inward + speed); SOLAR as a relative colour-bar - height proportional to the round's solar normalised across all rounds (lowest round still shows a small bar), each bar a SOLID colour interpolated deep-red at the event max to pastel-yellow at the min, no scale/labels. LEGEND top-right as a colour key with SQUARE swatches: Bill Maisey (green), 'Round Leader (<name>)' with the round leader's actual name (blue), and 'Regs limit / Other pilots' (grey - grey means both the regs cap on bullets and the field on the violin) - this replaces the per-round 'Bill vs leader' header text. Lay the dashboard as a 2-row x 4-column grid with the bottom row (laps/rank/wind/solar) aligned to the top row's columns
steps: Build score-violin, bullet, paired-bar, wind-card and solar-colourbar SVG components; assemble as the first per-round section

Test: renders the score violin (blue 1000 + green Bill over grey field density), four bullets (grey=regs cap or domain, blue leader, green Bill, green value on the right, no orange), a laps paired-bar, rank text, wind card, and a normalised red-to-yellow solar bar; works for triangle and speed rounds
